title: Day 706 — Sheinbaum Calls Fox a 'Traitor to Democracy' Over Alito Moreno Meeting, Pledges No New Taxes in 2027 Economic Package
detail: On September 7, 2026 (Day 706, Monday), back at the National Palace after her ten-state Second Government Report tour, President Sheinbaum sharpened her earlier criticism of the September 4 meeting between former president Vicente Fox and PRI national leader Alejandro "Alito" Moreno, mocking it as "the new vision of Mexican politics" and saying it would not go well for them. She called Fox a "traitor to democracy... seen by all Mexicans, first for the desafuero [2004 attempt to bar AMLO from the presidential race] and then for the 2006 electoral fraud," and accused PAN's younger leadership of ties to real-estate corruption scandals, arguing neither PRI nor PAN reaches double digits in support. Separately, ahead of the September 8 delivery of the 2027 Economic Package to Congress, Sheinbaum reiterated "no ha habido un aumento de impuestos ni va a haber" (there has not been a tax increase, nor will there be), saying additional revenue will come from combating tax evasion and shell companies used for false invoicing rather than new levies or new social programs, while keeping austerity in senior government salaries to fund existing welfare spending.

media.caption: Sheinbaum calls Fox a 'traitor to democracy' over his meeting with PRI's Alito Moreno

title: Day 706 — Sheinbaum Calls for US-Mexico Coordination After Trump Orders Review of Mexican Gray Wolf Protections
detail: At her September 7, 2026 mañanera, President Sheinbaum responded to President Trump's September 4 executive order "Supporting America's Ranchers," which instructed Interior Secretary Doug Burgum to determine within 90 days whether the gray wolf and Mexican wolf still meet criteria for Endangered Species Act protection. Sheinbaum said the cross-border, binational nature of the species — found on both sides of the Mexico-US border — requires a coordinated conservation strategy between the two governments regardless of any US decision, adding that Mexico maintains its own protections for the Mexican wolf under international conservation protocols. She raised the issue the same day Greenpeace activists occupied the Zócalo flagpole in Mexico City to protest a fertilizer/ammonia plant in Topolobampo, Sinaloa; Sheinbaum said community assemblies are ongoing to ensure the company meets its environmental commitments. She also clarified that the previous week's booing incident during her Colima tour stop was directed at a protester holding a megaphone, not at her.

media.caption: Sheinbaum calls for binational coordination on Mexican gray wolf protections after Trump's executive order
